case: ice-ridge keel grounding: dual (particle x mesh) convergence study

predeclared.decision: Can the ice-ridge keel grounding resistance be claimed converged, and if not, which discretisation blocks it and how many particles would be needed?
competing_alternatives: A1 the particle axis converges once four levels are used -- the legacy bond law is fine
A2 the legacy bond law has no particle-converged limit because kn is particle-size independent (k ~ kn/a ~ 1/a); the spacing-consistent law is required
A3 the mesh axis is the limiting one because the rigid platen edge makes the contact pressure discontinuous
predeclared.hypothesis: H1 the measured resistance is finite and mesh-converged (GCI < 5 %, order >= 1.5); H2 the legacy bond law gives no particle-converged limit while the spacing-consistent law restores one.

metrics.R_N_per_m: keel max penetration resistance at w0 (max over the ramp)
metrics.A_c_m2_per_m: keel contact area per unit out-of-plane width at w0
metrics.q_max_Pa: peak keel contact pressure at w0

predeclared.baseline_control: W27 (mission 18963): particle GCI 39.6 %, mesh GCI 0.077 % on the legacy bond law.  Arm 'spacing_consistent' changes exactly one variable (the bond stiffness length).
predeclared.stopping_rule: the predeclared 4 x 3 grid is run to completion; no level is added or dropped after inspecting numbers

controlled: keel height and patch aspect ratio
confounders: lattice coordination drifts slightly with particle count
the bond-length law changes the small-strain modulus by construction, so the arms are compared through convergence, not through absolute values
the platen edge is a contact-pressure discontinuity: a uniform mesh family is not in the asymptotic range at the coarse level

predeclared.repetitions: deterministic quasi-static solver, no time-integration noise; the repetition axis is the discretisation ladder (4 particle levels, 3 mesh levels) with two triads evaluated per axis
predeclared.analysis: Roache GCI on the finest triad of each axis with the other axis at its finest level; observed order reported in the particle count (r = 2) and in the physical spacing (2 p), Richardson limit with a 1.25 safety band, monotonicity check on every triad
predeclared.environment_limits: cluster job; one Python process per (arm, particle level); wall-clock recorded in the artifact

limitations: the keel is a bonded lattice with frozen topology (strain ~4e-3): no bond breakage, no block rotation, no rate effects; the freeze-bond modulus 1 GPa is a stiffness choice, so absolute pressures are model dependent -- the *convergence* statements are not
the structure is a plane-strain beam (unit width) with free ends; the overhang past the contact area lifts off (no-tension) and is not carried by buoyancy
the local keel constitutive law entering the coupled solve is the confined (wide-lid) compression curve; footing edge effects enter only through the reconciliation block
the rigid-platen edge makes the contact pressure discontinuous, which caps the observed order of the uniform mesh family (remedy demonstrated with a platen-edge-graded family, reported separately)
the no-tension switch is smoothed with a C1 ramp of width 0.1 w0; the ramp sensitivity block shows the spread (see extra_evidence.ramp_sensitivity)
ISO 19906:2019 A.8 and IACS UR I values are WITHHELD: no standard number enters any computation in this artifact
